newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says will not urge softening of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says will not urge softening of EMU criteria.

text.p: Italian prime minister Romano Prodi said on Monday he would not ask for a weakening of the criteria for joining Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and that there was no need to delay Italy's entry.
Prodi was speaking at a news conference after holding talks in Munich with Bavarian prime minster Edmund Stoiber, one of Germany's staunchest advocates of a hard single currency.
"I fully trust the fact that Italy be ready for next spring. I wont ask for any delay of Italy's EMU entry," Prodi said.

He added: "Italy is a country that, unlike Germany, is totally in favour of the euro. I am not here to discuss Maastricht criteria, we need to get out of uncertainty and Germany too needs to get certainty."
Stoiber told reporters: "I welcome the fact that Prodi told me he wanted to stick to the criteria for EMU entry."
Prodi is scheduled to travel to Frankfurt where he will hold a news conference at 1530 GMT or 1600 GMT before meeting leading German business representatives at a dinner hosted by Commerzbank AG.

Prodi's visit, which follows an official visit to Bonn on February 7, comes amid speculation that Germany does not want Italy in EMU from the start because of fears its membership may weaken the euro and make it harder to persuade Germans to give up the mark.

Senior bankers have recently warned of turmoil in the financial markets if Mediterranean countries like Italy, whose currencies have been less stable than the mark, were allowed to help launch the euro.
Meanwhile Stoiber has voiced doubts about Italy's ability to fulfil the stability criteria strictly.

In a television interview earlier this month, Stoiber said accepting creative accounting to allow countries to join EMU meant that "we'll never succeed in having the Italians and the Spanish and the Portuguese (keep to) a strict application of the stability criteria."
